PERFORMANCE TESTS FOR COMPLETE, FlLLED TRANSPORT PACKAGES
PART 9 STACKING TEST USING COMPRESSION TESTER

( First Revision)
0. FOREWORD
0.1 This Indian Standard ( Part 9 ) ( First Revision Bureau of Indian Standards,on 14 May 1987, after the Transport Packages Sectional Committee had Marine, Cargo Movement and Packaging Division ) was adopted by the the draft finalized by been approved by the Council,

0.2 This Indian Standard first published in 1975, has been revised to bring it in line with the revised IS0 2874-1985 `Packaging - Complete, filled transport packages - Stacking test using compression tester' published by the International Organization for Standardization ( IS0 ). This revision incorporates the following changes: a) The specification of the compression slightly ( see 3 ), and b) A new clause on `package preparation' tester has been modified has been added.

0.3 This test may' be used to assess the performance of a package in terms of its strength or the protection which it offers to its contents when it is subjected to stacking. It may be performed either as a single test to investigate the effects ( deformation, creep collapse or failure ) of this hazard or as part of a sequence of tests designed to measure the ability of a package to withstand a distribution system that includes a stacking hazard. 0.3.1 The test may also be used to investigate performance under specific conditions of loading, as for example, when ,the bottom package in a stack rests on an open-decked pallet. When the compression load is not to be applied over the whole surface of the package which is being tested, appropriate devices should be suitably interposed between the package and platen of the press in order to simulate the conditions met in practice when applying these compression loads.

1. SCOPE 1.1 This standard ( Part 9 ) specifies a method of carrying out a stacking test on complete, filled transport packages, usicg a compresson tester.

APPARATUS 3.1 Compression Tester - motor driven, mechanical platen-type, capable of applying load through uniform one or both platens. 3.1.1 The platens shall be: or hydraulic, movement of package on the lower platen of a compression upper platen to impose a load upon it. 3.1.2 One platen shall remain horizontal, within 2 parts in 1 000 at alf times during the test.

3.1.3 The other platen shall be either rigidly mounted so as to remain horizontal within 2 parts in 1000 at all times during the test, or be held by a tiniversal joint at its centre and so be free to tilt in any direction.

3.3 Meaus of Imposing a Predetermined Load - for a predetermined time, without fluctuation exceeding f4 percent and with no more relative movement of the platens than is necessary to maintain this load during any vertical displacement of the upper platen. 3.4 Means of Measuring Deflection ( If necessary ) - accurate to rtl mm and capable of indicating either an ixrease or a decrease in dimensions. 4. PACKAGE PREPARATION 4.1 The test package shall normally be filled with its intended contents. However, simulated or dummy coctents may be used on the condition that the dimensions and physical properties of such contents shall be as close as possible to those of the intended contents. 4.2 Ensure that the test package is closed normally, as if ready for distribution. If simulated or dummy contents are used, ensure that the normal method of closure IS still employed. 5. CONDITIONING 5.1 The package shall be conditioned in accordance conditions described In 1s : 7i)31 - 1987*. 6.
